judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The image is the featured thumbnail of a teaser card in the 'Artigos mais recentes' carousel (hands breaking chalk over a faint '1968'). The card itself carries the headline 'Gestão Tarcísio exonera professoras com regra da ditadura', an excerpt, and category, date and author. The thumbnail is an editorial illustration of that headline, and the model itself says it 'represents the theme'. Nothing in it is needed to understand or use the card, so alt="" is acceptable for this kind of decorative teaser image, and the incidental '1968' does not make it informative content. The card's real defect is a different one: its stretched link (#post-267202 > a) has no accessible name (2.4.4/4.1.2). That has nothing to do with this image's alt text.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is a stock-style photo of a phone showing the e-Título app with an error dialog. It is the thumbnail of a teaser card whose headline ('Plataformas mantêm anúncios e recomendações políticas irregulares no dia da votação') and excerpt carry the story. The error text in the photo is incidental illustration, not information the card needs to convey, so alt="" on a decorative teaser thumbnail does not fail 1.1.1. The card's empty stretched link is a separate issue under another criterion.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The page title 'Flávio Bolsonaro e os esqueletos no armário' is a shortened form of the H1 ('Flávio Bolsonaro e o risco de um presidente com esqueletos no armário'), and the live page still has it. It clearly describes the topic of this column. 2.4.2 does not require the site name or the full headline, so the claim that it 'says nothing about this page' is wrong.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is an inline citation link in the column. The live HTML and the snapshot's readingText give the sentence as 'A jornalista Flávia de Oliveira chamou a atenção para o fato de que, por conta da ação de André Mendonça...'. Under 2.4.4 the purpose can be determined from the link text together with its enclosing sentence (G53), and the sentence makes clear that the link points to the source where Flávia Oliveira made this point (it goes to her O Globo column). So the claim that 'nothing around it' tells the purpose is false. The snapshot's own paragraph 'text' field reorders the link words ('...Oliveira a atenção ... chamou por conta...'), which may have misled the model, but readingText was correct.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is an inline source link in the sentence '...pela empresa Entre Investimentos, que lavava inclusive dinheiro para o crime organizado...'. It goes to a CNN Brasil report on that company's ties to organized crime. Read with its enclosing sentence (the programmatically determined context 2.4.4 allows), its purpose is clear: it is the source for the claim that the company laundered money for organized crime. A more descriptive link text would be better practice, but the link does not fail the AA criterion.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The h5 'Assine nossas newsletters' heads a bordered call-to-action box placed mid-column. The box contains only an 'Assinar' button to the newsletter signup (screenshot confirms), so the heading accurately describes its own content and purpose. The article paragraphs that follow in DOM order are not that heading's content, and an interjected heading level is at most a 1.3.1 structure concern, not a non-descriptive heading under 2.4.6.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The h2 'Aviso' ('Notice') heads a one-sentence notice: 'Este é um conteúdo exclusivo da Agência Pública e não pode ser republicado.' (live HTML and screenshot). The heading names the section's purpose: it is a notice. 2.4.6 does not require headings to be long. The suggested replacement 'Apoie a Agência Pública' shows the model misread which content sits under the heading.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: #other-amount is a number input (min 10) at the end of a row of preset donation amounts (R$ 25 ... R$ 500), and its only label is the placeholder 'Outro valor'. In that context 'Outro valor' (other amount) says exactly what to enter, so the 2.4.6 claim fails. A placeholder-only label could be raised under 3.3.2 or 1.3.1, but that is a different claim from the one made here.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: In the footer menu under 'Republicação', the link 'English' (to /category/english/) has no lang attribute, and the live HTML shows none on its li, ul or ancestors, so it inherits html lang="pt-BR". The text is the name of a language written in that language, which is the case the 3.1.2 Understanding document uses as its example: alternative-language links should carry lang, e.g. Deutsch. None of the exceptions (proper name, technical term, indeterminate language, vernacular) applies, so this is a real failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The footer link 'Español' (to /category/espanol/) has no lang attribute on itself or any ancestor, so it inherits pt-BR. It is a Spanish word (Portuguese would be 'Espanhol') used as a language-version link, the pattern the 3.1.2 Understanding document gives as needing lang (it even cites a span containing 'Español' with lang="es"). No exception applies, so it fails 3.1.2 as reported.
